key_insight: A multi-protein blood/CSF signature can stratify ALS survival better than clinical features alone, highlighting biology linked to disease progression.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this proteomic panel could help enrich ALS trials and support more individualized prognosis using objective biomarkers.
method: Longitudinal proximity extension assay proteomics on 1,095 serum and CSF samples from 426 people with ALS
Age- and sex-adjusted Cox analyses to find proteins associated with survival
Penalised Cox regression and joint modelling to build and test prognostic protein panels
evidence_signal: The abstract reports discovery in 426 ALS patients with orthogonal replication in an external cohort of 349 patients, including a 9-protein serum panel that improved survival prediction over clinical models and NEFL alone.
watch_item: The panel needs broader external validation and careful standardization before routine clinical use, especially across different centers and sampling conditions.
paper_title: A proteomic signature for prognostic stratification in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
